target.name: NetworkOcean
target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a seed-stage company in the ocean and maritime sector, founded by serial entrepreneur Sam Mendel and ex-Palantir engineer Eric Kim. The valuation exercise draws on a small private comp universe of three peers (Standard Subsea, Clippership, Albacore), with no direct public comparables available in this nascent subsector.

The analysis applies a stage-progression method, using the company's $1M total raised as a proxy base value. Applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $2M. This methodology is the sole triangulation approach applicable given data constraints and the early-stage, pre-revenue nature of the business.

The triangulated range is $2M (low) to $3M (high), with a median of $2M. This narrow band reflects limited methodological coverage—only one valuation approach was feasible—and the substantial uncertainties inherent in pricing an early-stage frontier-tech company. Key risks to the range include execution capability of the founding team (mitigated by prior exits and technical depth), product-market fit validation in maritime applications, and regulatory or capital intensity of the underlying ocean technology sector. Additional revenue traction, customer pilots, or expanded comp data would narrow this range materially.
